newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MALDINI DENIES POSSIBLE MOVE TO CHELSEA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MALDINI DENIES POSSIBLE MOVE TO CHELSEA.

text.p: AC Milan and Italy left back Paolo Maldini has denied speculation linking him with English premier league club Chelsea, who already employ three of his compatriots.
Maldini acknowledged in an interview with sports daily Gazetta Dello Sport that Chelsea player-manager Ruud Gullit and Milan's acting president Adriano Galliani were in regular contact.
However, Maldini added: "Gullit and Galliani ring one another regularly but as far as I know there has never been an official or serious offer from any club.
"My contract runs out in the year 2001 and I intend to stay at Milan, but of course it takes two parties to settle these matters."
Gianluca Vialli, Roberto de Matteo and Gianfranco Zola are the Italian trio who joined London side Chelsea this season.
Maldini, meanwhile, is preparing to return for Milan against Fiorentina on Saturday following a two-match ban after being sent off during a 1-0 loss to Perugia.
He regards his dismissal as just one more unfortunate incident in a disastrous season for the side who have dominated the last decade of Italian soccer.
"When you start the season badly, it is difficult to immediately recover," he said.
"Then the more you play, the more the results don't go your way, the more certain negative tensions begin to weigh heavily."

Although Milan face Saturday's game in 12th position, just seven points clear of the relegation zone, Maldini does not rule out a recovery that would bring his team back into contention for a UEFA place next season.
"The league table has been very odd, I've never seen anything like it in recent years, all you need is two wins and you are back up in the UEFA zone," he said.
